name: support_resistance_reversal_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: NIFTY's previous day high and low are the most-watched reference levels by all algorithmic market makers, institutional desks, and retail momentum traders simultaneously — making them genuine order-flow anchors, not arbitrary lines. When NIFTY probes the previous day's high, option writers (covered call desks, prop short-gamma positions) and fresh put buyers cluster limit orders within 15-25 spot points of that level, creating a dense supply wall that materialises as range contraction at 5-second resolution. At 5s granularity, we detect the micro-structural 'probe-and-reject' signature: price approaching within 0.15% of the prev day level, range contracting over the last 30 seconds (accumulation of resting limit orders), and a visible 15-second rejection move in the opposite direction — all before the full 1-minute bar closes. BANKNIFTY amplifies this effect due to 2-3x higher volatility, so the same proximity threshold generates larger option moves.

indicators.name: prev_day_high
indicators.formula: previous session's daily high, computed by grouping spot_df by day_id and shifting
indicators.purpose: The key S/R reference. Previous day high is a fixed daily reference, not a rolling window — no scaling needed. Acts as resistance: institutional sell programs and stop clusters rest just above this level.

indicators.name: prev_day_low
indicators.purpose: Previous day low as support level. Institutional buy programs, delta-hedging by put writers, and stop-loss reversals cluster at this reference. No scaling — this is a fixed date-level anchor.

indicators.name: range_6
indicators.formula: mean(high - low) over last 6 bars (30 seconds)
indicators.purpose: 30-second average bar range. Captures range contraction as price is squeezed against the S/R level by accumulation of limit orders on both sides. 6 bars (30s) chosen because micro-coiling at S/R happens in seconds on NIFTY — longer windows would include the approach phase and miss the contraction signal.

indicators.name: range_prior_6
indicators.purpose: Baseline range from the prior 30-second window. Comparing to range_6 detects whether current activity is contracting (less volatile = limit orders absorbing flow at S/R) versus approaching (still moving directionally). Lookback of 12 bars (60s) total gives one comparison window of 30s each — sufficient context without including noise from earlier in the session.

indicators.name: ret_3
indicators.purpose: 15-second return to detect the initial reversal candle. 3 bars (15s) is the shortest window that filters single-bar noise (individual 5s prints can be erratic). A positive ret_3 near support signals actual bid absorption; negative ret_3 near resistance signals offer take. The original's HL reversal pattern took 5 one-minute bars (5 min); we compress to 15 seconds because we want to enter at the BEGINNING of the bounce, not after confirmation.

conditions: range_6 < range_prior_6 (range contracting — limit orders absorbing at support)
ret_3 > 0.0002 (first visible bounce in last 15 seconds)
vix < vix_max (default 20.0) — S/R levels respected in low-volatility regimes
buy_ce.confirmation: All four conditions simultaneously on same 5s bar

conditions: range_6 < range_prior_6 (range contracting — limit orders at resistance creating supply wall)
ret_3 < -0.0002 (first visible rejection in last 15 seconds)
buy_pe.confirmation: All four conditions simultaneously on same 5s bar

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points through the S/R level. A genuine S/R reversal should not allow 8 spot points of adverse penetration — if the level breaks by that much, stop-cascade selling begins and the thesis is definitively wrong. At delta 0.5 on ATM option, 8 spot points = 4 option points.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points = ~14 NIFTY spot points bounce. NIFTY S/R reversals at prev day H/L typically extend 15-25 spot points before meeting next intraday resistance. Target of 7 captures ~60% of the lower-bound bounce (14 of 25 spot points), giving 1:1.75 risk-reward without being greedy enough to give back the move.

filters.vix_filter: vix < 20.0 (S/R levels break rather than reverse in high-VIX regimes; NIFTY trends through levels when VIX > 20)
filters.time_filter: 09:20-15:25 IST (skip first 5 minutes of noise; first valid prev_day_high/low requires at least 1 completed session)
filters.volume_filter: none (NIFTY index volume is noisy at 5s; range contraction serves as the flow signal instead)
filters.trend_filter: none (S/R reversals are by definition counter-trend; trend filter would eliminate the setup)
filters.spread_filter: none (limit order execution, no spread cost)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — S/R levels are crowded; if too many algos pile in, levels break more often than bounce

adaptation_notes: Original trades nifty200 stocks at 1-min bars with multi-day S/R identification and HL reversal pattern (5-bar pattern = 5 minutes). Three key changes: (1) Universe shifted to NIFTY index using prev day H/L — cleanest, most liquid institutional S/R reference. (2) HL reversal pattern (5-min) compressed to ret_3 (15-second) — we want entry at bounce start, not confirmation. (3) Relative volume filter dropped — index volume at 5s is too noisy; replaced by range contraction which captures the same limit-order accumulation signal without the stock-level vol data requirement. VIX filter retained from original at same threshold (20).
weaknesses: Trending days: when NIFTY is trending strongly, prev day H/L breaks rather than bounces — stop-cascade through these levels is especially violent
First trading day of data has no prev_day reference — those bars are excluded
NIFTY levels can be probed multiple times before reversing — multiple consecutive triggers may be required before a clean reversal fires
Range contraction can also precede breakouts (false reversals) — especially after 14:00 IST when institutional positioning is being unwound
